items.prompt:
About how old is Earth?
A) 4.6 thousand years
B) 4.6 million years
C) 4.6 billion years
D) 46 years

steps: Earth is about 4.6 billion years old.

items.prompt:
Rock strata are:
A) Layers of sedimentary rock
B) Types of fossils
C) Kinds of planets
D) Ocean currents

steps: Strata are layers of sedimentary rock.

items.prompt:
In undisturbed rock, the oldest layers are:
A) At the top
B) At the bottom
C) Floating
D) Missing

steps: Lower (deeper) layers formed first and are oldest.

items.prompt:
How do fossils help match rocks of the same age?
A) They glow
B) The same fossils in different places mark rocks of the same age
C) They are all the same
D) They move between layers
items.answer: B) The same fossils in different places mark rocks of the same age

steps: Matching fossils indicate rock layers of the same age.

items.prompt:
The geologic time scale is used to:
A) Predict the weather
B) Organize Earth's long history into named divisions
C) Measure distance
D) Weigh rocks
items.answer: B) Organize Earth's long history into named divisions

steps: It organizes Earth's enormous history into eras and periods.

items.prompt:
If layer A is below layer B in undisturbed rock, then layer A is:
A) Younger
B) Older
C) The same age
D) Not a rock

Why is a geologic time scale necessary?
A) Earth has no history
B) Earth's history is enormous and must be organized to describe when events happened
C) Rocks have no layers
D) Fossils are useless
items.answer: B) Earth's history is enormous and must be organized to describe when events happened

steps: Dividing the vast history makes it possible to describe events in time.

items.prompt:
How do rock strata record the order of Earth's events?
A) Randomly
B) Each layer formed at a certain time, so the sequence of layers records events in order
C) All at once
D) They do not
items.answer: B) Each layer formed at a certain time, so the sequence of layers records events in order

steps: The ordered layers preserve the sequence of events over time.
